# Remote Control Server protocol

<!-- Generated by tools/offline_check/run.sh --update-protocol from the command definitions in
     RegisterCommands (RemoteControlServer.cs) and tools/offline_check/protocol_header.md. Edit those, not this file. -->

The same command definitions are in machine-readable form in `protocol.json`, and from a running server with
`Describe commands`.

## Messages

- One ASCII command per message: the command name, a space, then its arguments, e.g. `SetMagnetDAC 5.1` or `SetDeflection AX,100`.
- Command names are case sensitive.
- Numbers use `.` as the decimal separator.
- Every command gets exactly one reply: a value, `OK`, or a line starting with `Error:`.
- A running server lists its commands with `Help`, and describes one with `Help <command>`.

### Discovering a server

Send `Describe` on connecting. It replies with JSON on one line:

```json
{"protocol":1,"version":"20.2","instrument":"HelixSFT","transport":"udp","tag_data":true,
 "features":["keepalive","subscribe","request_ids","scan_count","describe"],
 "detectors":[{"id":"CUP 1","name":"H1"},{"id":"CUP 0","name":"AX"},{"id":"CDD 0","name":"CDD"}]}
```

`protocol` goes up when a command or reply changes in a way clients must handle. `Describe commands` returns every
command definition: several kB, so use TCP. A server without `Describe` replies `Error: Invalid Command`.

In `protocol.json` and `Describe commands`, each command has:

- `args`: `name`, `type` (`number`, `integer`, `word` with no spaces, `text` which may contain spaces, or `enum` with
  `values`), `optional`, `repeated` (values are comma separated) and `separator`, the character before the argument.
- `reply`: `type` is one of the reply types below, with `unit` for a number and `of` for a list or stream.
- `hardware`: true when the command uses the hardware and so runs one at a time.

### Reply types

Any command can also reply with an error instead.

| Type | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ok` | `OK` | |
| `text` | `HelixSFT` | |
| `bool` | `True` | `True` or `False` |
| `number` | `5.1` | |
| `list` | `1.5,2.5` | comma separated |
| `lines` | `Ar\rAr_CDD` | separated by carriage returns |
| `scan` | `H2,0.1,AX,2.5` | `name,value` pairs when `tag_data` is true, otherwise values only |
| `counted_scan` | `1234\|H2,0.1,AX,2.5` | scan count, `\|`, then a `scan` |
| `stream` | | one line per item until the client disconnects |

### Request ids

Any command can start with `#<id> `. The reply then starts with the same id: `#42 GetMagnetDAC` → `#42 5.1`.
If the same client sends the same id and command again within `Config.request_id_window` ms (10 s), it gets the cached
reply and the command is not run again, so retrying a UDP request is safe.

### UDP

Send the command as one datagram; the reply comes back to the sending address and port. A trailing CR or LF on the
command is ignored. The reply has no line ending: the datagram is the reply.

### TCP

By default a connection carries one command: connect, send the command, read the reply until the server closes the
connection. The reply has no line ending. A client that sends nothing is dropped after `Config.tcp_read_timeout` ms (5 s).

If the first command on a connection is

- `KeepAlive` – the server replies `OK` and keeps the connection open. Commands end in CR, LF or CRLF. Every reply ends
  in LF, and only LF ends a reply, because `lines` replies contain CRs. The connection is closed after `Config.tcp_idle_timeout` ms (60 s) without a command.
- `Subscribe` – the server writes `<scan count>|<data>` and a newline for every scan until the client disconnects.
  `Subscribe` is also allowed after `KeepAlive`.

Commands that only read the server's own state (scan data, `GetMagnetMoving`, `Ping`, `Help`, `Describe`, `GetVersion`) answer at
once. Commands that use the hardware run one at a time.

## Errors

| Reply | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Error: Invalid Command` | No such command |
| `Error: missing argument for <command>` | |
| `Error: invalid number in <command>` | |
| `Error: could not read <parameter>` | Qtegra could not read the parameter, usually because the name is not in the hardware database |
| `Error: could not set <parameter> to <value>` | |
| `Error: unknown detector <name>` | Not in the detector names configured for the instrument |
| `Error: magnet is moving` | A `SetMagnetDAC` or `SetMass` move is still running |
| `Error: timeout` | `GetNextData` saw no new scan in time |
| `Error: no data` | No scan received yet |
| `Error: <message>` | Anything else; the details are in the Qtegra log |

## Finding parameter names

`GetParameter`, `SetParameter`, `Open`, `Close` and `GetValveState` take the name of an item in the instrument's
hardware database, e.g. `Field Set`, `Y-Symmetry Set`, `CDD Supply Set`, `Deflection AX Set`.

- **Hardware database file**: `C:\ProgramData\Thermo\Qtegra\_Application Data\PluginData\<instrument>\<instrument>.imhwd`
  on the instrument PC. The Hardware Configurator in Qtegra's Configurator tool shows the same items.
  `tools/list_parameters.py` extracts candidate names from that file.
- **Check names against a running server**: `CheckParameters <name>,<name>,...` replies `True` for each name Qtegra can
  read. `python3 tools/smoke_test.py <host> --parameters <file>` checks a whole list.
- **Scripting manual**: the Qtegra Scripting Language Software Manual (P/N 1383460) lists the Helix SFT hardware items
  in chapter 3.
- `ProbeInstrument` logs what the instrument object exposes, to look for a way to list the parameters from the script.
